ai.subject: Anatomy
ai.summary: The neck contains several fascial triangles that organize muscles, vessels, nerves, and lymphatics. Understanding their borders helps locate pathology and plan procedures.

b: Anterior triangle: bounded by SCM, midline, and inferior belly of omohyoid.
Posterior triangle: bounded by SCM, trapezius, and clavicle.
sections.p: The deep cervical fascia forms two main triangles: the anterior and posterior triangles, each further divided by the sternocleidomastoid (SCM) and the omohyoid muscles.

b: Anterior triangle sub‑triangles (e.g., carotid, muscular, submandibular) house the carotid sheath, thyroid, and infrahyoid muscles.
Posterior triangle sub‑triangles (e.g., occipital, supraclavicular) contain the spinal accessory nerve, brachial plexus roots, and supraclavicular lymph nodes.
sections.p: Each triangle contains characteristic structures that guide clinical assessment and interventions.
